# A planar centroid dual bound and the full identical-endpoint edge family

This note gives an explicit stronger planar constant in the ordinary
dominated-density centroid inequality. It then proves the requested
edge credit at the TRUE mixed centroid for identical endpoint bodies,
including every triangle-plus-identical-slabs family from the preceding
counterexample. Arbitrary distinct endpoints are not reduced to this
case.

## 1. Ordinary planar theorem with an explicit dual certificate

Let K be a planar convex body, let 0<=eta<=1_K dx be a finite measure,
and let g be the centroid of rho=1_K dx+2eta. Then every closed
halfplane H containing g satisfies

    |K intersect H|+eta(H)
       >= c_* rho(K),       c_*=6144/22745>4/15.          (1)

No shape or regularity restriction is placed on eta. This is an
ordinary planar statement, with no discrete-lattice conclusion built
into it.

Normalize |K|=1 and write alpha=eta(K). It suffices to consider a
halfplane through g, since parallel inward translation can only reduce
its measure. Domination gives 0<=alpha<=1 and absolute continuity of
eta. Since rho has density at least one on K, g is in its interior:
every nonconstant supporting linear functional has average strictly
less than its maximum. Thus a through-g halfplane has ordinary area
s in(0,1). Set r=eta(H).

Here are the needed cap-quantile steps explicitly. For the scalar
projection X in the cap direction, let V(t)=|K intersect{X>=t}| and
G(t)=sqrt(V(t)). The cap midpoint inclusion and planar Brunn--Minkowski
make G concave on the projection interval. The projection law has a
continuous strictly positive interior density, so V(X) is uniform on
[0,1] under ordinary volume. The pushforward of eta has a density
h(v) between zero and one, with integral alpha and integral over[0,s]
equal to r. Jensen at the actual rho centroid gives

    (1+2alpha)sqrt(s)>=2/3+2 integral_0^1 sqrt(v)h(v)dv.

For an increasing integrand and a density bounded above by one,
placing a prescribed mass at the left end of an interval minimizes
the integral. This follows by subtracting the corresponding interval
indicator and then subtracting the value at its right endpoint from
the integrand. Apply this separately on[0,s] and[s,1]. The resulting
intervals fit because r<=s and alpha-r<=1-s. Therefore

    integral sqrt(v)h(v)dv
      >=(2/3)[r^(3/2)+(s+alpha-r)^(3/2)-s^(3/2)].       (2)

Define

    U=1/s, E=r/s, Q=(s+alpha-r)/s,
    phi(t)=t-(2/3)t^(3/2), t>=0.

Then U>=1, 0<=E<=1, Q>=1. Dividing the preceding inequalities by
s^(3/2) and using alpha=s(Q+E-1) gives exactly

    phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)>=2/3.                        (3)

This is the same necessary scalar relation as in the archived general
density-sandwich proof; the new step here is its planar dual choice.
For any real a and t>=0, elementary one-variable maximization gives

    phi(t)+a t <=(1/3)(1+a)_+^3.                      (4)

Indeed the interior maximizer, when a>-1, is t=(1+a)^2; otherwise the
maximum is attained at zero. Put

    D=U+2Q-(7/4)E.

Apply(4) with a=1/2 to U and Q, and with a=-7/16 to E, retaining
their respective multiplicities one, two, two. It yields

    phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)+(1/2)D
       <=(1/3)[3(3/2)^3+2(9/16)^3]
       =7155/2048.

Combining with(3),

    D<=17369/3072.                                    (5)

Finally the exact mass identity and E<=1 give

    (1+2alpha)/(s+r)
       =[U+2Q+2E-2]/(1+E)
       <=[11225/3072+(15/4)E]/(1+E)
       <=22745/6144.                                  (6)

For the last inequality the displayed ratio increases with E, since
15/4>11225/3072; substitute E=1. This proves(1). Hyperplane boundaries
have zero area and eta mass throughout; no closed-halfplane boundary
case is discarded. The exact comparison with 4/15 follows from
6144*15-4*22745=1180>0.

## 2. Application to the true mixed centroid, including every ambient tilt

Let A,K be planar convex bodies with A subset K, |A|=v>0,
|K|=kv, and 1<=k<=3. Put copies of A at bases -1 and 1, and K at
base zero. These are the exact integer fibers of their convex hull,
which has nonempty ambient interior. Let Y=(0,g) be their true mixed
centroid. Its base coordinate is zero by the equal endpoint masses;
its continuous coordinate g is exactly the centroid of

    rho=1_K dx+2 1_A dx.

In particular g belongs to K, so Y is a single actual mixed point.
For an ambient through-Y halfspace with nonzero continuous normal,
write its traces as

    u.x>=u.g+beta       on the left A,
    u.x>=u.g            on K,
    u.x>=u.g-beta       on the right A.

At least one endpoint trace contains A intersect{u.x>=u.g}; the other
has nonnegative area. Consequently(1), with eta=1_A dx, proves

    D_S(Y)>=c_*(k+2)v>(k+1)v/3
              =(3/4)Gamma_2(|K|+|A|).                (7)

The strict comparison holds uniformly for 1<=k<=3: the difference
between the first and second expressions in(7) decreases with k, and
at k=3 it is

    [5c_*-4/3]v=(1180/68235)v>0.

A pure integer halfspace through Y contains K and one full endpoint,
of mass(k+1)v, which also dominates the bound c_*(k+2)v. A halfspace
containing Y can be translated parallel to itself until its boundary
passes through Y. Thus(7) covers every closed ambient halfspace,
including oblique ones and those with the whole middle fiber on the
boundary. No expectation or direction-dependent center is used.

If the endpoints are translates of A, the affine shear aligning them
preserves the mixed lattice, every fiber area, and ambient halfspaces.
It carries their true mixed centroid to the centroid just used, so the
same conclusion holds for translated copies with a compatible middle.

This proves the entire identical-slab family, with arbitrary slab
placement and all k in[1,3], at the particular centroid used in the
counterexample. In fact it allows arbitrary A and arbitrary containing
K. It does not assert that arbitrary independent endpoint profiles can
be replaced by one common dominated eta while preserving their
centroid and every tilted cap. The separate actual coupling theorem
supplies exactly the replacement needed for the following extension.

## 3. Arbitrary equal-area endpoints by the proved midpoint coupling

Let A,B be arbitrary planar convex bodies of the same area v>0, and
let K contain (A+B)/2. The dominated midpoint coupling theorem,
proved directly in
`accepted fact 486fe778f838d99d, f6641f09c19819a3`,
gives one measure eta<=1_K dx of mass v and centroid(g_A+g_B)/2.
Every actual midpoint in a through-y middle halfplane has at least one
coupled endpoint in the corresponding two tilted endpoint halfplanes.
Integrating this pointwise statement shows that their actual area sum
is at least eta of that middle halfplane, with closed boundaries kept.

The true mixed centroid is Y=(0,g), with

    g=[|K|g_K+v(g_A+g_B)]/(|K|+2v).

It is exactly the centroid of 1_K dx+2eta, and belongs to K. Applying
(1) to every nonvertical through-Y halfspace and handling pure integer
halfspaces by their mass |K|+v gives the unconditional bound

    D_S(Y)>=(6144/22745)(|K|+2v).                       (8)

Here |K|>=v by Brunn--Minkowski, so the pure integer cap ratio is at
least2/3, exceeding c_*. Thus(8) controls every closed ambient
halfspace at one actual point for arbitrary equal-area endpoint
shapes. For |K|<=3v it also gives the strict edge inequality(7), with
the same positive original-mass surplus. The later all-dimensional
mass-dependent dual proves the edge target for every d>=1; it does
not replace the larger explicit planar normalized constant in(8).
